{{short description|Type of topological space}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Parovicenko space''' is a [[topological space]] similar to the space of non-[[isolated point]]s of the [[Stone–Čech compactification]] of the [[integer]]s.

==Definition==
A Parovicenko space is a topological space ''X'' satisfying the following conditions:
*''X'' is [[compact space|compact]] [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]]
*''X'' has no isolated points
*''X'' has [[weight of a topological space|weight]] ''c'', the [[cardinality of the continuum]] (this is the smallest cardinality of a [[base (topology)|base]] for the [[topological space|topology]]).
*Every two disjoint open [[F-sigma set|''F''<sub>σ</sub>]] subsets of ''X'' have [[disjoint sets|disjoint]] [[closure (topology)|closures]]
*Every [[empty set|non-empty]] [[G-delta set|''G''<sub>δ</sub>]] of ''X'' has non-empty [[interior (topology)|interior]].

==Properties==
The space β'''N'''\'''N''' is a Parovicenko space, where β'''N''' is the [[Stone–Čech compactification]] of the [[natural number]]s '''N'''. {{harvtxt|Parovicenko|1963}} proved that the [[continuum hypothesis]] implies that every Parovicenko space is isomorphic{{clarify|reason=what is meant here by "isomorphism"? homeomorphism?|date=January 2021}} to β'''N'''\'''N'''. {{harvtxt|van Douwen|van Mill|1978}} showed that if the continuum hypothesis is false then there are other examples of Parovicenko spaces.
